title: Ynot v. Intermediate Appellate Court
summary: The Supreme Court declared Executive Order 626-A unconstitutional for authorizing the summary confiscation of carabaos transported across provincial boundaries without due process. While the ban on carabao slaughter was valid, the confiscation penalty was an unreasonable and oppressive exercise of police power.
doctrine: While the State may validly exercise police power to regulate the slaughter and movement of carabaos, the outright confiscation of the animals without giving the owner a hearing violates procedural due process. The penalty must bear a reasonable relationship to the purpose of the regulation.
fullText:
CRUZ, J.:

The petitioner challenges the constitutionality of Executive Order No. 626-A which provides for the immediate confiscation of carabaos being transported from one province to another.

The police power is not unlimited. While the ban on the interprovincial transportation of carabaos may be a valid exercise of police power to preserve the work animals needed for agriculture, the penalty of confiscation without the benefit of a prior hearing is a denial of due process.

The due process clause applies to the exercise of police power. Even in the legitimate exercise of police power, the means employed must be reasonably necessary for the accomplishment of the purpose and must not be unduly oppressive upon individuals.
